result.topic_en: A table showing how multiples of the prime 37 arise as sums of two squares, followed by a remark that proving that the quotient 1 always appears would complete the proof of Fermat's theorem on primes of form 4n+1, and the statement and start of the proof of Theorem 65: no sum of two coprime squares is divisible by a prime of form 4n−1.

116 RESIDVA EX DIVIS. POTESTATVM

Diuisor 37 ... | 1 | 4 | 9 | 16 | 25 | 64 | 81 | 100 | 225

fumma | 37 | 148 | 333 | 185 | 74 | 185 | 370 | 296 | 481
quotus | 2 | 4 | 9 | 5 | 2 | 5 | 10 | 8 | 13.

Si igitur demonftrari poffet in his quotis femper vnitatem reperiri, haberetur demonftratio completa Theorematis Fermatiani, quod omnis numerus primus formae $4n+1$ fit fumma duorum quadratorum. Quoniam vero alibi demonftraui fummam duorum quadratorum inter fe primorum alios diuifores non admittere, nifi qui ipfi fint fummae duorum quadratorum; demonftratio iam pro abfoluta eft habenda, quae multo conciunior eft ea, quam olim per plures ambages elicueram. Sin autem fimul perpendamus, in quotis illis nullos numeros primos formae $4n-1$ occurrere poffe, vti mox demonftrabitur, haec demonftratio forte multo magis contrahi poterit.

Theorema.

65. Nulla fumma duorum quadratorum inter fe primorum per vllum numerum primum formae $4n-1$ diuifibilis exiftit.

Demonftratio.

items.quote: Si igitur demonftrari poffet in his quotis femper vnitatem reperiri, haberetur demonftratio completa Theorematis Fermatiani, quod omnis numerus primus formae $4n+1$ fit fumma duorum quadratorum.
items.english: If therefore it could be proved that unity is always found among these quotients, a complete proof of Fermat's theorem would be had, that every prime number of the form 4n+1 is a sum of two squares.

items.quote: Sin autem fimul perpendamus, in quotis illis nullos numeros primos formae $4n-1$ occurrere poffe, vti mox demonftrabitur, haec demonftratio forte multo magis contrahi poterit.
items.english: But if we consider at the same time that no primes of the form 4n−1 can occur among those quotients, as will soon be shown, this proof can perhaps be shortened much further.

items.quote: Nulla fumma duorum quadratorum inter fe primorum per vllum numerum primum formae $4n-1$ diuifibilis exiftit.
items.english: No sum of two squares that are coprime to each other is divisible by any prime number of the form 4n−1.
